taera_intro.title: Earth
taera_intro.narrator: Taera. Bearer of Earth. What she carries.
taera_intro.text:
Earth smells of yesterday's rain.

Even when it hasn't rained.

It holds on to scents for a long time.

That's why I love digging.

To find what's left.

choices.text: What does it hold on to?

taera_ce_quelle_garde.title: What the Earth Keeps
taera_ce_quelle_garde.text:
Everything.

Seeds we forgot to plant.
The roots of trees we cut down.
The footprints of people who left.

Earth has a longer memory than people do.

When I touch the ground somewhere,
I feel what happened there.

Not clearly.

Like a vibration.

A house that has welcomed a lot of people
vibrates differently from an empty house.

A battlefield vibrates differently from a garden.

My mother thought I was making it up.

My brother thought I was strange.

My father thought it was a gift.

taera_enfance.title: The Garden
taera_enfance.text:
We lived in the mountains.

Not very high.

Just high enough to see the plain below.

My father grew vegetables.

Not to sell.
To eat.
For the neighbors.
For the ones who had none.

He used to say:

**"The earth gives to those who give to it."**

I had my hands in the dirt every day.

Cold in the morning.
Warm in the afternoon.
Damp after the rain.
Dry in summer.

I learned its moods
before I learned to read.

taera_pere.title: Taera's Father
taera_pere.text:
My father had hands like roots.

Broad.
Strong.
Covered in soil even after he'd washed.

He didn't talk much.
But when he did,
it was always at the right moment.

In the evening he'd sit at the edge of the garden.
He'd look at what had grown.

He didn't count.
He didn't measure.

He just looked.

Once I asked him what he saw.

**"What was there before."**
**"And what will be there after."**

I didn't understand.

Now I do.

It's exactly what I see too.

taera_decouverte.title: The First Time
taera_decouverte.text:
I was six.

A tree had fallen in the storm.

Old.
Huge.
It blocked the road to the neighboring village.

The men were trying to move it.
Impossible.

I was standing there watching them.

I put my hand on the trunk.

Just to touch it.

And the tree moved.

Not much.
Just enough to make everyone stop.

The men looked at me.

I looked at my hand.

The bark was warm.
As if the tree were still breathing.

taera_reaction_village.title: The Village
taera_reaction_village.text:
Badly.

Not violently.

But the looks had changed.

The village women crossed themselves when I walked by.
The children stepped aside.

My mother came to take me by the hand.
She smiled at the others.
She held my hand tight.

Both at once.

**"You only do that at home now."**

**"But I didn't do it on purpose—"**

**"I know."**

She held on even tighter.

**"I know."**

I understood that my mother had two fears.
Fear for me.
And fear of me.

It took me a long time to accept
that both could exist at the same time.

taera_reaction_elle.title: Her Reaction
taera_reaction_elle.text:
Curious.

Mostly curious.

The tree was heavy.
I could feel it.
As if its weight ran through my arms.

But it wasn't unpleasant.

Like lifting something important.

I'd put my hand back on the trunk.

Nothing.

Again.

The tree had trembled.

I'd smiled.

Then my father arrived.
He'd seen my hand on the tree.
He'd seen my smile.

He said nothing.

That evening he taught me how to plant seeds.

As if it were the logical next step.

taera_apprendre.title: Learning on My Own
taera_apprendre.text:
My father taught me to garden.

He didn't know that's what he was doing.

But planting a seed and watching it grow —
it's exactly the same motion as holding a sword
and feeling the earth answer back.

Give before taking.
Wait before acting.
Listen before speaking.

I did that for two years.

Without naming it.
Without understanding everything.

Just doing it.

The earth doesn't ask questions.
It answers what you give it.

taera_limites.title: Limits
taera_limites.text:
I found one.

Just one, really.

If I gave too much —
without resting,
without letting the earth regenerate —

I'd collapse.

Not physically.

Inwardly.

Like a field that's been overplanted.

After too much effort,
I'd sleep for two days.
Hands stuck to the earth.
As if I needed to be recharged.

My brother would find me there in the morning.

He wouldn't say anything.
He'd lay a blanket over me.
And then he'd go finish the rest of the work.

That's how we communicated.

He and I.

Without words.

taera_recrutement.title: The Woman of Stone
taera_recrutement.text:
She arrived one autumn morning.

A woman.

Tall.
Dressed in brown and green.

She smelled of forest after rain.

She stopped in front of our garden.

She looked at the earth.

Then she looked at me.

**"You talk to the earth."**

**"It answers me."**

She seemed satisfied.

**"How long?"**

**"Since I was six."**

**"And you weren't afraid."**

**"No."**

**"Why?"**

I thought about it.

**"Because the earth doesn't hurt people who listen to it."**

She smiled.

**"True."**

taera_femme_peur.title: Not Afraid
taera_femme_peur.text:
No.

She smelled of forest.

People who smell of forest
usually don't do harm.

It's a rule I'd made up myself.

Probably not very reliable.

But it had held so far.

What surprised me was her gaze.

She looked at me as if she knew something
I didn't know yet.

Not pity.
Not suspicion.

Just: *I know where you're going.*

It was both reassuring and terrifying.

taera_depart_famille.title: The Departure
taera_depart_famille.text:
My father listened to the Woman of Stone.

For a long time.

My mother was quietly crying in the kitchen.

My brother was standing against the wall.
Arms crossed.
Like Ikar, now that I think about it.

At the end my father stood up.

He went out into the garden.

I followed him.

He picked up a handful of earth.

He put it in my hand.

**"Will you keep it?"**

**"Yes."**

**"Good."**

He went back inside.

I held the earth tight in my palm.

I still have it.
In a small pouch.
Around my neck.

taera_frere.title: The Brother
taera_frere.text:
He hadn't said a word the whole conversation.

When I came out with my bag,
he was standing in the doorway.

He handed me something.

A small stone.
Round.
Gray.
Smooth, as if it had spent years in a river.

**"It's from the garden."**

**"I know."**

**"It was under the tree you moved when you were six."**

I looked at him.

**"You remember that?"**

**"I always watched when you did weird things."**

He shrugged.

**"To see if it was dangerous."**

**"And?"**

**"No."**

He went back inside.

I put the stone in the pouch with the earth.

It's still there.

taera_aurenthal.title: Aurenthal
taera_aurenthal.text:
Aurenthal smelled of stone and crowds.

Not unpleasant.

Just different.

The Temple smelled of old wood and incense.

The other three were waiting.

The silver-haired girl was staring at her hands.

The boy with burns on his forearms had said:
**"You're late."**

Not to me.
To the silver-haired girl.

I'd smiled at her anyway.

He didn't smile back.

The other boy — eyes everywhere — had waved at me.

**"I'm Vael."**

**"Taera."**

**"Did you travel long?"**

**"Three days."**

**"Me, five."**
**"The mountains are far."**

He knew where I came from without my saying it.

I found that kind.

taera_ikar_debut.title: Ikar — The First Day
taera_ikar_debut.text:
He was difficult.

Not mean.

Difficult.

He took up too much room in conversations.
He decided before we'd finished talking.
He acted before we'd finished thinking.

The second week I set bread down in front of him.

He looked up.

**"You don't eat in the morning."**

**"How do you know?"**

**"The earth knows when someone is empty."**

He looked at the bread.
Then at me.
Then at the bread.

He ate without a word.

The next day there was firewood outside my door.

For the night fire.

He didn't tell me why.

It was his way of saying thank you.

That's how we learned to talk to each other.
Without words.
Through gestures.

In the end, not so different from my brother.

taera_entrainement.title: Training
taera_entrainement.text:
The Spirit of Earth was called Mael.

Old.
Very old.
She smelled of humus and wet stone.

She taught by doing.

Not by talking.

We planted together.
We dug together.
We lifted together.

One day she let an enormous boulder drop.

**"Lift."**

I lifted it.

**"Higher."**

**"I can't."**

**"You haven't tried."**

I had tried.

I lifted it higher.

**"Again."**

**"I'm going to fall—"**

**"Then fall."**

I fell.

**"Good."** she said.
**"Now you know how far you can go."**

The earth had cushioned my fall.

Of course.

choices.text: Did she talk to you about the others?

taera_mael_autres.title: Mael and the Others
taera_mael_autres.text:
Sometimes.

She spoke of them as elements.

**"Fire is impatient."**
**"Water is patient."**
**"Air is elusive."**

**"And earth?"**

**"Earth is present."**

**"That's all?"**

**"That's a lot."**

She planted a seed.

**"Be present."**
**"Fully there."**
**"Not in yesterday."**
**"Not in tomorrow."**
**"There."**

**"That's your role in this group."**

**"Being there?"**

**"Being there when the others can no longer be."**

I didn't understand at the time.

Now I understand perfectly.

taera_pret_a_tout.title: Ready for Anything
taera_pret_a_tout.location: Temple of the Order — Common room
taera_pret_a_tout.text:
It was our third year.

Mael had gathered all four of us.

She said:

**"The bearer of Chaos will come."**
**"You must be ready for anything."**

Ikar said yes without hesitation.

Aryn looked at her hands.

Vael pretended to look somewhere else.

I said:

**"No."**

Everyone turned around.

Mael looked at me.

**"No, what?"**

**"No, I won't be ready for anything."**
**"There's always another way."**
**"We either search long enough, or we don't search long enough."**

Silence.

Mael nodded.

**"Good."**

Ikar said:

**"Good how?"**

She didn't answer.

taera_pourquoi_non.title: Why No
taera_pourquoi_non.text:
Because the earth doesn't destroy what it can nourish.

That's its nature.

It can crush.
It can bury.
It can block.

But it doesn't burn.
It doesn't cut.
It doesn't kill if it can do otherwise.

I am the bearer of Earth.

My nature is to find another path.

Even if it takes longer.
Even if it's harder.
Even if everyone thinks it's impossible.

The seed in the stone.

Everyone thinks it's impossible.

The seed knows otherwise.

taera_ikar_apres.title: Ikar Afterward
taera_ikar_apres.text:
He caught up with me in the hallway.

**"You're naive."**

**"Maybe."**

**"There isn't always another way."**

**"I think there is."**

**"And what if you're wrong?"**

I turned around.

**"Then I'll be the first to admit it."**
**"And you'll do what you have to do."**

He said nothing.

**"That's why there are several of us."** I added.
**"You can do what I can't."**
**"And I can try what you rule out."**

He nodded.

Not agreeing.

But he understood.

That was enough for me.

taera_annees.title: The Years
taera_annees.narrator: Ten years old. Eleven. Twelve. Thirteen.
taera_annees.text:
We grew up.

My garden at the Temple grew too.

I had laid out a patch of courtyard.

No one asked me to.
I just did it.

Ikar would come by sometimes.
He'd sit down.
He wouldn't say anything.

Aryn came when she was thinking too much.
Water and earth got along well.

Vael never really came.
But sometimes in the morning I'd find little flowers
that the wind had brought.

That the wind had brought.

Of course.

taera_jardin_autres.title: The Garden of the Four
taera_jardin_autres.text:
The garden had become their way of being there
without having to talk.

Ikar came when he was angry.
The earth absorbed it.

Aryn came when she doubted.
Plants don't doubt.

Vael came... I wasn't sure why.

One evening I asked him.

**"Why do you come here?"**

**"Your garden smells nice."**

**"Is that all?"**

He looked at the plants.

**"Here everything grows."**
**"Even fragile things."**

He left.

I understood.

Vael felt fragile sometimes.

And in my garden, that was allowed.

taera_mael_vieille.title: Mael
taera_mael_vieille.text:
Spirits don't really age.

But Mael was becoming rarer.

Less present.

As if she were saving her strength.

One evening she stayed in the garden for a long time.

**"Are you leaving?"** I asked.

**"Soon."**

**"After him?"**

She knew who I meant.

**"Maybe."**

**"And what if we don't make it?"**

She placed her hand on the earth.

**"The earth remains."**
**"After everything."**
**"Always."**

**"Is that supposed to reassure me?"**

**"It's supposed to give you perspective."**

She vanished.

I planted a seed where her hand had been.

It bloomed.
It still does.

taera_veille.title: The Signal
taera_veille.location: Temple of the Order — Garden — Night
taera_veille.text:
I felt it in the earth.

Not suddenly.

Like a distant vibration.

The ground trembling slightly.
Not an earthquake.

The signature of an enormous power
somewhere to the west.

I was in the garden.
I'd just planted the autumn seeds.

My hands were in the soil.

And the earth told me:

*now.*

I stood up.

I washed my hands.

I took the pouch from around my neck.

My father's earth.
My brother's stone.

And I went to wake the others.

taera_reveille_ikar.title: Waking Ikar
taera_reveille_ikar.text:
He was already up.

Of course.

Fire had warned him before me.

He was buttoning his armor.

**"You felt it too."**

**"Yes."**

**"Ikar."**

**"What."**

**"We try first."**

He looked up.

**"That's what you always say."**

**"And I'll say it again tonight."**

He seemed about to say something.

He fastened his armor.

**"I know."**

It was the first time he'd said *I know*
without arguing.

The earth had shivered under my feet.

Slightly.

A good sign.

taera_reveille_aryn.title: Waking Aryn
taera_reveille_aryn.text:
Her light was on.

She was staring into her basin.

**"You felt it."**

**"Yes."** she said.
**"He's alone."**

**"How do you know that?"**

**"Water knows."**

She looked up.

**"Taera."**

**"Yes."**

**"He's afraid."**

**"I know."**

**"Ikar is going to—"**

**"I talked to him."**

She looked back at her basin.

**"Do we have time to save him?"**

The earth beneath my feet.
Still that vibration.

**"I think so."**

**"Do you think, or do you know?"**

**"I think."**

She nodded.

For Aryn, that was enough.

taera_depart.title: The Departure
taera_depart.text:
Four silhouettes in the courtyard.

It was still night.

Vael was whistling.

**"Stop."** said Ikar.

**"Why?"** said Vael.

**"Because."**

**"Solid argument."**

I placed my hand on the courtyard floor.

The Temple's earth.

Cold.
Ancient.
Full of everything that had happened here before us.

All the generations who had set out from here
before us.

Some never came back.

**"Let's go."** said Ikar.

I tightened my pouch.

My father's earth.
My brother's stone.

And we set off.

taera_route.title: The Road
taera_route.text:
Earth under the horses' hooves.

Every village we passed.

I could feel it changing.

Fertile near the rivers.
Dry on the plateaus.
Heavy around the old forests.

And the closer we got —

The stronger the vibration.

Not aggressive.

Wounded.

Like a tree that's been pruned too hard.
Still trying to grow,
but in any direction at all.

**"Are you all right?"** Vael asked.

**"He doesn't seem malicious."**

**"How do you know?"**

**"The earth tells you when someone wants to do harm."**
**"This is different."**
**"This is someone who wants to help."**
**"And doesn't know how."**

Vael looked at the road ahead.

**"That's worse, in a way."**

**"Yes."** I said.
**"That's why we won't stop him."**
**"We'll help him."**

taera_fumee.title: The Smoke
taera_fumee.text:
We saw the smoke.

I placed my hand on the ground from my horse.

Difficult.
But possible.

The vibration was there.
Strong.
Painful.

But beneath it —

Something gentler.

Shame, perhaps.
Pain.

Not violence.

**"He's still there."** said Aryn.

**"He's alive."** I confirmed.

Ikar had been staring at the smoke.

For a long time.

**"Let's go."** he said.

I tightened my pouch one last time.

My father's earth.
*The earth gives to those who give to it.*

My brother's stone.
*To see if it was dangerous.*

It wasn't dangerous.

It was painful.

That's different.

taera_derniere_pensee.title: What She Carried
taera_derniere_pensee.text:
The pouch around my neck.

My father's earth.
My brother's stone.
The dried flower from Mael's garden.

And something I had put inside
without really deciding to.

A seed.

I didn't know what kind.

I had picked it up in the Temple garden
the morning we left.

Just a seed.

To remind me that even in places
that have lost everything —

something can still grow.

If someone takes the time to plant it.

fin_memoire_taera.title: Ending — Taera's Memory
fin_memoire_taera.text:
The memory settles gently.

Like earth after the rain.
